name: Backstab Fish
description: Backstab Fish is a high-octane, multi-deck evolution of the classic Go Fish. Designed for large groups (up to 10 players), it utilizes two full decks and four Jokers to create a chaotic environment where memory and deception are paramount. Unlike the child's version, Backstab Fish features aggressive 'Quantity Bidding' and rules that allow players to 'backstab' opponents by stealing specific duplicates or utilizing Jokers as wild 'spies'.

history.origins: Backstab Fish is a modern large-group variant of Go Fish, played with two decks and four jokers. It builds on 19th-century quartet and Go Fish family games but scales them for louder, more competitive tables.
timeline: 19th Century: 'Authors' and other quartet games establish the core 'ask and take' mechanic.
Mid 20th Century: Single-deck 'Go Fish' becomes a widely played children's game using standard packs.
Modern era: Backstab Fish is played in Adelaide, Australia, using 108 cards and quantity-based asking.
Present: Played as a loud, social party variant for large groups that keeps the memory and book-collecting core of Go Fish.
history.cultural: Around Adelaide tables it is treated as a vocal, social deduction variant where calling specific opponents and quantities is part strategy and part performance.
history.evolution: Backstab Fish takes the basic Go Fish structure and extends it to a 108-card pack, with players tracking up to eight copies of each rank and using quantity asks to swing large numbers of cards at once.

setup.dealing: For 4-6 players, deal 7 cards each. For 7-10 players, deal 5 cards each. The remainder forms the 'Ocean' (Stock).
setup.equipment: Comfortable seating where all players can be heard clearly.

rules.objective: Collect the most 'Books' (sets of 4 cards of the same rank). Each Book is worth 1 point.
rules.gameplay: Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn you make an enquiry: name a specific opponent and ask for a specific number of cards of a rank of which you hold at least one (e.g. give me three sixes). If that player has the exact number requested, they hand over those cards and you get another turn. If they do not have enough cards of that rank (e.g. they only have two sixes), you draw one card from the stock (the Ocean) and your turn ends; the turn then passes to the player you asked. You are not required to lay down a complete set of four as soon as you have it; you may keep cards in hand to ask for more of that rank, but if you do not lay them down another player may ask you for them and take some or all away. Completed books may be laid face up. When the stock is empty and play finishes, the player with the most books wins.
keyRules: Completed Books must be played immediately face up.
If a player runs out of cards, they draw a full hand from the stock (if available).
Two decks mean there are EIGHT of every rank (two potential books per rank).

strategy.basic: Memory is everything. Pay close attention to what other players are asking for, even when it isn't your turn. If Player A asks Player B for 7s, you now know both players likely have 7s.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Re-Fishing' Tactic: If you know someone just fished a card you originally held, wait until they've collected a few more of that rank before asking them. Let them do the work for you.
strategy.advanced: Quantity Bluffing: Ask for a rank you only have one of, but do it confidently as if you are completing a Book. This clears the 'Ocean' of that rank as others stop fishing for it, thinking you've already cornered the market.
tips: Don't hold onto a Joker too long. Use it to complete a Book and get it out of your hand before someone 'fishes' it from you.
If the Ocean is small, fishing is more effective than asking. The probability of a hit increases significantly in the late game.

variations.name: Full Backstab
variations.description: Players can ask for a card by rank AND suit. This makes the game move much slower but increases the 'memory' stakes.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is descriptive only for now; engine values match the main rules and no numeric overrides are required yet.

scoring.winCondition: Highest number of books at the end of the stock.

synthesis.shortDescription: Think Go Fish is for kids? Think again. Backstab Fish ups the ante with double decks, Jokers, and high-capacity play. It's a game of social deduction, advanced memory, and strategic theft where reaching into the 'Ocean' is just the beginning of the hunt.
